ruling.recommended_action: Refer to Ryde human review to establish whether the driven off-route segment corresponds to the route the rider agreed to (RD-5/G13); hold the $6.94 meter refund pending that finding.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeTAXI ride, so mileage enters the fare directly and any unexempted off-route kilometre is refundable at this trip's rate: $31.30 ÷ 22.20 km = $1.4099/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The trace has settled the RD-4 screen: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced optimal stretch reported before the detour — the AYE breakdown at 09:47 [F15] and the band-2 record ending at 10:13 [F12] do not cover the 10:13–10:24 segment, and a speed band alone never exempts [F3][RD-4]. The only possible exemption left is rider consent under RD-5.

Reading the chat: the driver asked at 10:10 "mind if I go round via Clementi Avenue 2?" [F8], and the rider answered at 10:10 "Sure, your call." [F9]. The rider's message is a genuine agreement sent before the segment started at 10:13, in a fully timestamped chat record [F10]. The question the trace leaves to me is its SCOPE. The driver's own proposal named a specific road, Clementi Avenue 2 [F8]; the rider's "your call" adopts that proposal rather than conferring a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation, because it answers a message that named a route. Under RD-5, an agreement to a specifically named road covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the driven segment to it. No fact places the car on Clementi Avenue 2: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3], and the driver's post-trip statement says only "I took another way," naming no road [F11]. Timing (10:10 before 10:13) alone does not tie the segment to the agreed road — exactly the gap G13 describes.

If the words were instead read as a general route authorisation, the segment would still be exempt only if it were a route chosen to get to Jurong East MRT; nothing in the record shows where the 4.92 km of extra driving went or what it reached, so even on that reading the record does not establish the character of the segment. Either way the record cannot settle whether the agreed route is the one driven, and this finding changes the amount (it decides whether $6.94 is refunded or nothing is), so under the trace's rule the case goes to a person rather than being ruled now. On the arithmetic, if it were found to count, the refund would be 4.92 km × $1.4099/km = $6.94 [F3][F4][RD-2]; the $0.13 metered waiting unit for 0.5 min is a RydeTAXI meter wait and is not refundable [F5][RD-3]. No account flag arises: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18], so RD-6's "repeated" condition fails [RD-6]. I record no safety concern: the chat, the complaint and the driver's statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][F10], and the RD-3 stop question is moot because no stop was measured in the segment [F3].
